value: Challis, C., Tierney, M., Todd, A. and Wilson, E. (2017). Human factors in dairy industry process control for energy reduction. Journal of Cleaner Production 168, 1319-1334. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jclepro.2017.09.121

Ethnographic/interview study of control-room operators at two UK dairy sites, focused on pasteurisation. No technology-level energy figures of its own. Numbers it has, reprinted from the Carbon Trust IEEA dairy guide (CTG033, cited as 'Carbon Trust n.d.'): pasteurisation 30-40% of site process energy; excess hot-water recirculation (>10 min) raises specific pasteurisation CO2 by 16-18%; two sites with regenerator efficiency 93% (2.5 kgCO2/m3) and 88% (3.55 kgCO2/m3); +1% regeneration efficiency saves about 0.2 kgCO2/m3 (about GBP 10,100/yr for 350,000 m3/yr). Fig. 2 (dairy subsector energy-intensity ranges) is reproduced from the Carbon Trust guide as an image. Partly relevant to the to-get row 'Carbon Trust 2010 (IEEA guide to the dairy sector, CTG033)' but only as a citing sibling; that row is NOT satisfied.
